{{Quote|Nobody expects the Imperial Inquisition!|[[Fa'Zoll]]|<ref name="SWG:JtL">''[[Star Wars Galaxies: Jump to Lightspeed]]''</ref>}}
The '''Inquisitorius''', also known as the '''Imperial Inquisition''', or the '''Inquisitor's team'''<ref name="Master of Deception" /><ref name="Reckoning">''[[The Last of the Jedi: Reckoning]]''</ref>, was a secret division of [[Imperial Intelligence/Legends|Imperial Intelligence]] consisting of [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] agents known as '''Inquisitors''' (sometimes also as '''Inquisitioners'''), or "truth officers".<ref name="CNII:SOS">''[[Coruscant Nights II: Street of Shadows]]''</ref>

Under the control of [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] and [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], these Inquisitors were considered the highest ranking of the [[Dark side adept/Legends|Dark Side Adepts]], outranking the [[Emperor's Hand/Legends|Emperor's Hands]], [[Prophets of the Dark Side]], and lesser [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]]. Reporting directly to the [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] or the [[Supreme Commander (Galactic Empire)/Legends|Supreme Commander]], they were officially classified as part of Imperial Intelligence however, still outranked a bulk of the Galactic Empire's ranks. For a time, they were made subservient to [[Ferus Olin]].

Some Inquisitors such as [[Laddinare Torbin]], [[Antinnis Tremayne]], [[Jerec (Inquisitor)|Jerec]] and [[Adalric Cessius Brandl|Adalric Brandl]] would use the prefix of [[Lord/Legends|Lord]].

==History==
{{Quote|The Inquisitors are the Emperor's shadowy agents. They are among those whom the Emperor calls his Dark Side Adepts. Chief among their duties is to hunt, capture, and interrogate Jedi. Some of the Inquisitors may even be former Jedi themselves. While classified as part of Imperial Intelligence, the Inquisitorius division reports directly to Emperor Palpatine.|[[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Wullf Yularen/Legends|Wullf Yularen]], ''[[Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''|<ref name="Imperial Handbook">''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''</ref>}}
The Inquisitorius was an organization established around [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]] by [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] Palpatine and [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] Vader. It consisted of Imperial Intelligence agents referred to as Inquisitors tasked with hunting down the last of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] in the aftermath of [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]].

[[File:Malorum.jpg|thumb|left|Maroon zeyd-cloth robes were standard for Inquisitors in the formative years of the Empire.]]
Potential Inquisitors were put through a rigorous selection process. First, they were extensively tested and examined by Imperial Intelligence, then by the [[Grand Inquisitor/Legends|Grand Inquisitor]], then by the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lords]] themselves.<ref name="ea:r2">''[[Evasive Action: Recruitment]]''</ref> Applicants had to prove themselves powerful and reliable.

While many Jedi fell in the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]], some, such as [[Antinnis Tremayne]] and [[Jerec (Inquisitor)|Jerec]], betrayed their order and joined the ranks of both the Inquisitorius and the Emperor's Dark Side Adepts. If an Inquisitor captured a Jedi, it was their job to make the Jedi turn to the dark side, and join Sidious' New Order. If the Inquisitor could not, it was their duty to eliminate the Jedi. Inquisitors would also search for non-Jedi Force-users to serve Sidious.

One of the first actions of the Inquisitorius was [[Flame Night]]. A nocturnal massacre of Force-sensitives and slaughter of innocents,<ref name="CNII:SOS" /> Padawans and other survivng Jedi<ref name="CNIII:POF" /> designed to rid the Empire of potential future threats as well as an attempt to draw out any surviving Jedi. By the standards of the Inquisitors, it had been a great success that received high praise from the Emperor.<ref name="CNII:SOS" /> The operation took place in Jedi Temple and also furthered the devastation of it as well, ensuring that it was ridden with rubble and covered with ashy dust and charred stone.<ref name="CNIII:POF" >''[[Coruscant Nights III: Patterns of Force]]''</ref> Flame Night was how [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Jax Pavan]] and [[Gray Paladin]] [[Laranth Tarak]] had met, they had barely escaped the ambush but Laranth had recieved two blaster wounds in the escape:<ref name="CNII:SOS" /> A scar on her cheek and ten centimeters of her left [[Lekku/Legends|lekku]] burned off.<ref name="CNI:JT">''[[Coruscant Nights I: Jedi Twilight]]''</ref><ref name="CNII:SOS" /> Following the operation the Inquisitors still lurked in the multifarious levels of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] in fewer numbers while most were sent to the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] and similar backplanets to find illegal Force activity. [[Den Dhur]], a former [[Journalist/Legends|reporter]], had heard that they could isolate a lone Force-sensitive, with either a newly formed connection or developed connection out of a population consisting of millions.<ref name="CNII:SOS" />

A Force-sensitive [[Unidentified Inquisitor (Cephalon)|Inquisitor]] within the first several months of the Empire was assigned to a [[Cephalon study|study]] with Imperial [[Scientist/Legends|scientists]]. The study focused on [[Cephalon|Cephalons]]. The study found that the four-dimensional beings had at least nine emotional states with possibly more. Three of the states were only faintly close to emotions experienced by other [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]]. Rumor had it that the study sent the Inquisitor mad while trying to wrap his head around the varying states of the Cephalons four-dimensional consciousness.<ref name="CNII:SOS" />

The Inquisitors were also responsible for awakening [[Arden Lyn]] after a twenty-five millennia long sleep. During this time, Inquisitor [[Valin Draco]] became involved in [[Sarlacc Project]], the secret construction of a prototype [[Super Star Destroyer/Legends|Super Star Destroyer]], showing that the order didn't focus solely on matters of the Force.

Following [[Battle of Endor/Legends|the first death]] of the Emperor at [[Endor/Legends|Endor]], the bureaucracy of the Inquisitorius engaged in infighting with other branches of the government to determine a successor, but some of Sidious's [[darksider]]s kept silent, knowing that the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] would return. Many Inquisitors joined the [[Pentastar Alignment]] under the title of [[Great InQuestor of Judgment]]. One of these was [[High Inquisitor]] Jerec, who attempted to gain control of the [[Valley of the Jedi]], but was foiled by the Jedi [[Kyle Katarn]]. 

Stripped of support and resources, most Imperial Inquisitors eventually disappeared from the galaxy. <ref>[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)'']]</ref>

After [[Battle of Onderon (Galactic Civil War)|the last death]] of the Emperor, the few surviving Inquisitors sent one of their failed apprentices, [[Brakiss]], to infiltrate [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker's]] [[Jedi Praxeum]] on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin IV]]. Luke realized what Brakiss was all along, but hoped to redeem him. When Brakiss eventually fled Yavin IV, he did not return to the Inquisitorius, but joined forces with [[Kueller]]. However, he did furnish the Inquisitorius with information about the Praxeum before vanishing. Years later, Brakiss formed a similar organization for training darksiders, the [[Shadow Academy]], under the [[Second Imperium]].

==Equipment==
Although they used lightsabers, Inquisitors could use [[Vibroblade/Legends|vibroblades]], [[Electrostaff/Legends|electrostaffs]], [[Force pike/Legends|force pikes]], [[Blaster pistol/Legends|blaster pistols]], [[DX-2 disruptor pistol/Legends|DX-2 disruptor pistols]], and [[DXR-6 disruptor rifle]]s for intimidation tactics or as primary or secondary weapons. Blaster pistols particularly were a favoured secondary weapon among many Inquisitors, with inquisitors such as Tremayne, [[Lanu Pasiq]], [[Gwellib Ap-Llewff]], [[Halmere]], and [[Drayneen]] favouring the ranged side arm even if in Tremayne's case it saw very little to no use. In some cases, such as High Inquisitor [[Mox Slosin]], his blaster pistol was his primary and only weapon.

==Operations==
{{Quote|You are an extension of my will.|Darth Vader, to his Inquisitors|<ref name="EA:R" />}}
The Inquisitors' primary purpose was the interrogation of Jedi or particularly resistant subjects. Subjects were attained for the Inquisitors by authorization of [[Legal Authorization for Advanced Confinement Document|LAACDocs]]. When usual methods of interrogation such as [[Torture/Legends|torture]] and [[Bavo Six]] injections failed to break a subject, Imperial Intelligence would call upon an Inquisitor, who would use powerful [[The Force/Legends|Force]] skills in conjunction with traditional but effective methods of manipulation to obtain success. In addition, several members of the Inquisitorius were themselves speculated to have been former Jedi.<ref name="Imperial Handbook" />

However, since Imperial Intelligence was quite effective in interrogating the average subject, they rarely required the services of an Inquisitor. Inquisitors instead spent much of their time looking for potential Jedi candidates using their specialization in [[Life Detection|life detection]] in the backwater parts of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], most often in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]], at the discretion of their leader the [[Grand Inquisitor/Legends|Grand Inquisitor]]. [[Malorum]], the first Grand Inquisitor, was killed on [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] by [[Ferus Olin]]. He was succeeded by the enigmatic [[Hydra (Grand Inquisitor)|Hydra]], who was tasked to assist Olin in locating [[Force Adept]]s, and came disturbingly close to discovering the Force-sensitivity of Princess [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] on [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]]. Lord Laddinare Torbin, the next Grand Inquisitor, was killed by an [[Assassin droid/Legends|assassin droid]] who crashed a [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttle]] into the Imperial palace on [[Weerden]] [[16 BBY/Legends|sixteen years prior]] to the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. The title was eventually taken up by the [[Zabrak/Legends|Zabrak]] [[Ja'ce Yiaso]]. The Inquisitorius, while classified as a branch of Imperial Intelligence, reported directly to Emperor Palpatine,<ref name="Imperial Handbook" /> or to the Supreme Commander,<ref name="kenner">{{KennerCite|set=Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (toy line)|pack=Darth Vader vs. Prince Xizor|link=soteKxizor-vader.asp}}</ref> [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Vader.<ref name="EA:R" />

The Inquisitorius was originally based on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], in the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] under Malorum and later in the Senate Tower under Hydra. Afterwards, the foreboding [[Citadel Inquisitorius]] was built on the planet [[Prakith/Legends|Prakith]] in the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]]; here, the High Inquisitors were given their assignments and conferred with their colleagues. Captured Jedi were imprisoned and tortured here. The Citadel's security was breached on at least one occasion, by allies of [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Organa]].

As of [[18 BBY/Legends|18 BBY]], all Inquisitors could be distinguished by enveloping, dark maroon robes of [[Zeyd-cloth/Legends|zeyd-cloth]] that invoked images of dark blood. This uniformity may have been discontinued with time.

They used [[Ultrachrome/Legends|Ultrachrome]] protection,<ref name="TJP">[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force (real-life book)|''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force'']]</ref> with [[Taozin amulet]]s creating a void in the Force so its wearer could not be detected by another Force-sensitive.<ref name="Imperial Handbook" />

Largely because of their secret nature in the Imperial Intelligence department, they received very few mentions even in the official field manual for the Imperial Military, ''[[Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]'', with [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], himself a Force-user, suspecting that the agency was kept secret by the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] due to their use of the Force, and also wondered if even the Imperial Military trusted them.<ref name="Imperial Handbook" />

The Inquisitor's would also be allowed to train apprentices, such as [[Probus Tesla]] training [[Renefra Ren]].<ref name="TLJ(N)">[[The Last Jedi (novel)|''The Last Jedi'']]</ref> However, Inquisitor's were also allowed to train Dark Jedi who were not officially apart of the Imperial Inquisition. Such as when the Inquisition found and trained [[Misha Vekkian]], who became an Imperial Dark Jedi and [[Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]].<ref name="AROW">{{DoD|A Reckoning of Wraiths}}</ref> Or when High Inquisitor Antinnis Tremayne trained a Dark Jedi, [[Vialco]].<ref name="UEK Sidebar">{{JournalCite|8|Uhl Eharl Khoehng (short story)}}</ref>

While scouting around at the [[ISB Central Office/Legends|ISB Central Offices]], Jax Pavan spotted three Inquisitors, one with a cowl, two with crimson robes, and sensed a dozen others wearing taozin.<ref name="CNIII:POF" /> Several months later when Jax and his team visited [[Bandomeer/Legends|Bandomeer]], there were one or two Inquisitors stationed there. Jax also passed another one or two Inquisitors when he infiltrated and was leaving the ISB. When Vader and most of the other Inquisitors left Coruscant shortly after Jax's snooping in the ISB, only four or five Inquisitors were left on Coruscant. Those four or five were the Empire's least experienced Inquisitors, some being Apprentice Inquisitors,<ref name="TLJ(N)" />

Additionally there were a couple sub-groups related to the Inquisitorius, such as the [[Inquisitorium dark trooper|Inquisitorium dark troopers]], [[Inquisitorium hunter|Inquisitorium hunters]],<ref name="SWG:Fotp" /> and additional agents serving the Inquisition, such as [[Blaise Zirkonn/Legends|Blaise Zirkonn]].<ref name="NOP">[[Nexus of Power]]</ref>

Inquisitors would also sometimes use the aide of more common people who could be useful, such as [[Zerala Dinn/Legends|Zerala Dinn]],<ref name="NOP" /> and [[Kunn Kuroosh]].

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:InquisitionBadge.jpg|thumb|right|200px|The Imperial Inquisition Ace Pilot Badge.]]
Agents of the Inquisitorius are most commonly known as "Inquisitors", but some sources such as [[Zirtran's Anchor (article)|''Zirtran's Anchor'']] use the term "Inquisitioner".

The term "Nobody expects the Imperial Inquisition!", is a reference to Monty Python's "Nobody expects the Spanish Inquisition!"

In ''[[Coruscant Nights III: Patterns of Force]]'' an [[Unidentified Imperial Force-sensitive|Imperial Force-sensitive]] who gets close to finding [[Kajin Savaros]] is heavily implied to be an Inquisitor though it isn't explicitly said.<ref name="CNIII:POF" />
